citation: Schroeder, Ken. "1.15 Improving the Mouth of the River." Chicago Architecture History, 9 February 2022.
author: Ken Schroeder
note: Carries the single most usable pair of elevation figures found for the original town site: the ground east of State Street lay nine to ten feet above the surface of the lake, while west of State Street it sloped down to the river in a level plain elevated only two to three feet above the river. Also the original soil profile of the business district (about 1 ft black loam over 3-4 ft of saturated fine sand over 8-12 ft of impervious blue clay) and the 1816 Long and 1830 Howard harbour proposals. Secondary synthesis by an architect-historian, not a primary survey; it gives no citation for the two-to-three-feet figure, which is why every elevation derived from it in this project is tagged inferred rather than documented.
access_notes: Reached through docs/research/01-terrain-hydrology.md, which quotes it verbatim. Not re-fetched at its locator by this parcel — the terrain values it supports are tagged inferred partly for that reason.
what_it_supplies: ground elevation of the plain west of State Street relative to the river
ground elevation of the ridge belt east of State Street relative to the lake
original soil profile of the business district
what_it_does_not_supply: a citation trail for its own elevation figures
